text:
Finn: quick thread — uploaded a small perf dump from yesterday's canary. noticed a sharp hit-rate drop for some mid-size tenants after the caching change. attaching numbers inline.

Finn: overall prefix-cache hit-rate went from 62% -> 41% for tenant group B during the 16:00-18:00 window. p95 latency for generations when cache missed rose ~18ms. cpu on serving hosts spiked.

Jess: ugh. did we change key derivation for the cache keys?

Finn: yes — the rollout removed the tenant-salt step to simplify cross-region lookup. code used to be: 
```python
key = HMAC(master_key, tenant_id || prefix)
cache_hash = sha256(key)
```
and we switched to `cache_hash = sha256(prefix)` to avoid pulling tenant metadata for every hit.

Emily: that explains collisions. without tenant separation different tenants can map to same cache entry, so visible hit-rate per-tenant is noisy and some tenants see 'bad' hits. also a security audit flag: cross-tenant leakage risk.

Sam: why did CPU spike though? removing the HMAC should reduce CPU.

Finn: right — expected less CPU. but what happened is increased cache churn + more remote fallbacks. more requests hit the cache key but belonged to different tenant contexts, so we lacked warm KV prefetch and the runtime ended up doing more model warmups and kernel rebinds. that triggered heavier compilation/select-kernel paths and higher per-request CPU.

Todd: interesting cascade. cross-tenant collisions -> wrong cached state -> model instance muxing changes kernel selection? can you paste profiler snippet?

Finn: snippet: 
```
19:03:12 | req 12345 | cache lookup: miss (collision detected)
19:03:12 | req 12345 | route -> fallback-variant (longer seq)
19:03:12 | kernel-chooser | recalc: selected aten_v2_fused (cold)
19:03:12 | kv-warmup | populate kv -> subsequent reqs fill with tenant A state
```

Jess: we should reintroduce per-tenant namespace but in a cheap way. options: (1) tenant prefix salt at key time (HMAC) but memoize per-tenant derived key in-memory; (2) HKDF with tenant-specific seed computed once per process; (3) store tenant-id alongside cache entry and check on lookup (cheaper to compute but doubles storage).

Emily: storing tenant-id on the entry is the simplest audit-friendly approach. on lookup we verify equality; if mismatch, treat as miss. That avoids crypto on the hot path. downside: extra metadata per entry and still increases storage I/O.

Sam: true. but our biggest concern is perf & privacy. for privacy we probably should encrypt cache values at rest with per-tenant key (AES-GCM). that has decryption cost on lookup though.

Todd: on decryption cost — we measured AES-GCM at ~200ns per block on our CPUs, but context switching and memory copies add overhead. For hot cache it adds up. Also encrypted entries make batching heuristics worse: we can't cheaply compare prefixes before decrypting, so batch dedup won't kick in.

Finn: here's a proposal from runtime perf POV: 
- reintroduce tenant scoping by storing tenant_id in the KV value metadata (cheap check on lookup)
- background job to re-hash hot prefixes into fully salted HMAC keys for faster lookup once warmed (lazy per-tenant memoized key)
- enable a 'soft-scope' flag in config so Dedicated customers can opt into HMAC at process startup (precompute per-tenant HMAC key using KMS-derived seed)
- for encryption: default to AES-GCM at rest but decrypt only on miss->serve path (keep non-decrypted routing metadata visible)

Jess: +1. can we measure the overhead of storing tenant_id and verifying before returning a cached response? need microbench.

OpsBot: scheduled perf job: cache-tenant-check-bench on eng-runtime CI. will run on next midnight fleet. (job id: run-5592) :gear:

Emily: audit note: Sec please run a scan for stale entries where tenant_id != expected mapping (we should detect entries where collisions caused mismatch).

SecBot: queued audit scan. scanning live caches across 5 regions. low-priority results expected in 6h. :mag:

Sam: another angle — kernel selection churn. if a collision returns a cached prompt that has different sequence-length distribution, the runtime may rebind kernels. Could we include light-weight metadata in cache (like expected seq_len bucket & model-arch tag) so kernel chooser can short-circuit? small extra cost but avoids recompute on miss.

Finn: good call. add a tiny header: {tenant_id, seq_bucket, model_tag} (bytes) so the kernel selector uses it to route to the right compiled path. non-sensitive.

Todd: warmup strategy: currently we do on-demand KV warmup by tenant on first miss. propose prioritized warmup: when a tenant's per-minute QPS crosses threshold, precompute salted keys and warm their hot prefixes into L1 cache (local memcache) and pin compiled kernels for expected seq_bucket. reduces flapping.

Jess: rollout plan? small canary first: re-enable tenant_id check + metadata, deploy to 10% of serving fleet for tenants in group B. measure: per-tenant hit-rate, p50/p95 latency, CPU delta, and collision counts.

Finn: agreed. metrics to capture: cache_true_hits (tenant-match), cache_cross_hits (tenant-mismatch), kernel_rebind_count, kv_warmup_ops, p99_inference_ms, and cost_delta.

Emily: also add an audit metric: stale_entry_ratio (entries older than X days with tenant tags).

Sam: baseline numbers captured. tagging this as P0 for perf-security combo. I'll own rollout and dashboard.

Todd: i'll prepare the microbench for tenant-id check and header parsing. planning to run on the same HW the canary uses.

Finn: thanks. anyone want to add other attack vectors? e.g., attacker crafting prefixes that hash to common entries to cause noisy neighbors?

Jess: yes adversarial key grinding possible. mitigations: HMAC with a secret per-fleet and rate-limit cache writes per-tenant prefix. also monitor entropy of incoming prefixes per tenant.

SecBot: noted. adding ruleset: rate-limit cache_writes per-tenant per-second, alert on prefix-entropy drop.

OpsBot: canary deploy scheduled: 1843219800 -> 1843223400 (2h window). will post results in this thread. :rocket:

Finn: perfect. thanks all. follow-ups: Sam will open rollout PR, Todd microbench PR, Sec will post audit results.

Jess: :thumbsup:

Emily: leaving a quick checklist comment in the PR for the tiny header fields.

Sam: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2845 (WIP)

Finn: closing loop — we should add a short doc on the tradeoffs (privacy vs latency) and link it in the PR. I'll draft it.

Finn: end.
